text: She considered lying.
speaker: Narrator

text: Instead she nodded once.
speaker: Narrator

text: He reminded me that people disappear faster than habits do.
speaker: Enhedu

text: No one had an answer for that.
speaker: Narrator

text: The wind shifted.
speaker: Narrator

text: Behind them, another ribbon of sand spilled over the ridge where the tomb lay buried once more.
speaker: Narrator

text: Kurash's absence sat between them like a fourth set of footprints that refused to fade. Every gust left fewer places where Kurash had ever walked.
speaker: Narrator

text: When they finally stopped, Balag dropped his gear and began checking the animals' hooves with the same methodical care he gave every practical task. Enhedu crouched a short distance away and cleaned dried blood from under her nails with the tip of her knife. The motion was precise, almost delicate.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik sat with his back against a low outcrop and stared at the linen wrapping on his left hand. The mark beneath it was quiet for the first time since the tomb. He did not trust the quiet.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag finished with the donkeys and came to sit across from him. The big man did not look at the journal.
speaker: Narrator

text: You counting the share already?
speaker: Balag

text: Balag asked.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Zik glanced up.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: What?
speaker: Zik

text: Kurash's share. You're sitting there doing the arithmetic in your head. I've seen that face before.
speaker: Balag

text: Zik almost denied it. Then he shrugged.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: If I don't, somebody else will.
speaker: Zik

text: The words came out harder than he meant. He heard how cold they sounded and hated himself for a second.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag just grunted.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Someone always does. Doesn't mean I have to like watching it.
speaker: Balag

text: He was quiet for a few breaths, then added, almost to the sand,
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: First crew I worked on, we lost a boy before we even reached the quarry. Fifteen years old. Same hungry look. Same fucking math.
speaker: Balag

text: He shook his head once.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Still don't like the sound of it.
speaker: Balag

text: Enhedu's knife paused.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: He would have done the same to any of us if the numbers came out that way.
speaker: Enhedu

text: Zik looked at her.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: That supposed to make it easier?
speaker: Zik

text: No. It's supposed to make it true.
speaker: Enhedu

text: They sat with that for a time. The desert cooled around them. Somewhere far off a night bird called once and did not call again.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag eventually stood and checked the straps on the packs a second time, even though nothing had shifted. Zik recognized the habit. The big man trusted his hands more than he trusted silence.
speaker: Narrator

text: We'll reach the city in two days if the weather holds,
speaker: Balag

text: Balag said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Collector's going to notice the missing man.
speaker: Balag

text: Let him notice,
speaker: Zik

text: Zik answered.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Enhedu wiped the last of the blood from her blade and slid it home.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: He'll notice the extra silver more.
speaker: Enhedu

text: Zik almost smiled. Almost.
speaker: Narrator

text: He opened the journal instead.
speaker: Narrator

text: The last page was still waiting. The three lines in his father's hand had not changed. The ink no longer looked wet, but the paper itself felt slightly warmer than the desert night should have allowed.
speaker: Narrator

text: He closed it again before anything new could appear.
speaker: Narrator

text: They slept in shifts. Zik took the middle watch. He spent it staring at the dark and listening for the low vibration they had heard beneath the tomb. It did not come. The mark on his palm stayed quiet. The compass, when he checked it, still pointed straight down.
speaker: Narrator

text: Toward morning Enhedu relieved him. She sat without speaking for a long time, turning a small copper figurine between her fingers the way other people turned prayer tokens. Time had polished its smiling face nearly smooth.
speaker: Narrator

text: You going to tell the Collector everything?
speaker: Enhedu

text: she asked eventually.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: No.
speaker: Zik

text: Good.
speaker: Enhedu

text: She tossed the figurine once and caught it.
